# Financial projection: Circadian (Verizon Smart Campus)

*Generated by `CFO_10K_MODEL.py`. Do not edit by hand; change assumptions in the model and re-run.*

## Bottom line
- **Base case, 2031 run-rate:** revenue $56.6M, EBITDA $20.7M (1.5 bps of FY2025 revenue; consolidated margin +0.0 bps).
- **5-year NPV (2027-2031, no terminal value):** $3.4M at 7.0%; IRR 18%; payback 52 months. With a terminal value (2% growth less churn, shared-savings fees ending with their 5-year contracts): $54.0M.
- **Software alone is not enough:** without Layer-4 network pull-through the 5-year NPV is -$4.1M. The pull-through ARR per customer is the number Verizon Business must validate first.
- **Range:** 2031 EBITDA -$3.0M (bear) to $140.8M (bull); 5-year NPV -$35.1M to $158.4M. Monte Carlo (4,000 draws, every assumption triangular): NPV P10 -$7.8M, P50 $1.5M, P90 $13.4M; P(NPV > 0) = 58%.
- **Context:** Enterprise & Public Sector revenue fell $684.0M in 2025 (10-K). The base case adds $56.6M of E&PS revenue by 2031, about 8% of one year's decline.
- **Honest scale check:** a ~21M/yr EBITDA business line by 2031, about 0.4% of the $5B 2026 opex-savings program. Not a moonshot: a product Verizon Business can pilot next year, whose network side makes AI energy saving cheaper on event days.

## What the simulator says about the network levers (calibration)
- Source: `prototype/out/sim_kpis.json`. Baseline = traffic-history AI with learned margins **plus the operator's manual event mode** (no energy saving on venue cells 2 h before to 4 h after a ticketed event).
- Extra radio energy saved by campus context, by day type: weekday -0.1%, gameday +7.0%, finals -0.4%, heatwave +0.2%, surprise +0.0%, arena +3.8%, snowday +2.5%, faultstorm -0.6%. Campus-year mix {'weekday': 300, 'finals': 14, 'gameday': 7, 'arena': 21, 'snowday': 2} -> **+0.29%**, the model's base value (bear 1.5x worse, bull 1.5x better). Small, as expected: context pays on irregular days only.
- One-off arena event: congested user-steps today's practice 14 vs Circadian 0: event mode already protects quality, so the event-day value is energy, not congestion. Care savings are therefore small in the model.
- Fault storm, 2,000 random draws: dispatches 5.73 -> 3.59 per 7 faults (**37%** avoided; no gain in 19% of storms); restore time 1241 -> 620 min. These follow from assumed dispatch and remote-fix probabilities.
- HVAC savings in the twin by day: weekday 11.6%, gameday 8.5%, finals 12.8%, heatwave 13.1%, surprise 11.1%, arena 11.5%, snowday 6.5%, faultstorm 10.8%. Almost all of it is ventilation by headcount. Planning uses the literature range 5%-10% (base 7%), not the twin.

## Upside options (excluded from every scenario above)
| Option | Math | Annual value |
|---|---|---:|
| Network-wide context on Verizon's ~60,000 vRAN sites (public event + school calendars) | RAN electricity $0.65-1.10B (est) x 30% of sites x 0.3% extra saving | $557k-$942k |
| Student acquisition at partner campuses | 90 campuses x 15,000 students x 0.5 pt share gain x $900 contribution (all est) | $3.0M-$9.1M |
| Verizon as customer zero: occupancy-driven HVAC in Verizon's own offices | Not sized - Verizon does not disclose office energy; 10-Q cites +$114M Q1-26 building costs | not sized |

The first row is why radio energy is not the headline: even network-wide, context adds single-digit millions on top of the AI energy saving Verizon already runs ("over $200 million", Schulman, Q1-26 call).

## Carbon

- Customer HVAC emissions avoided ('enabled' reductions, not Verizon's own inventory), 2031: 91,636 tCO2e at 0.325 t/MWh.
